p_l:
CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 38-year-old female presenting with blurred vision and worsening visual disturbance that began approximately three days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as progressive and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for type 1 diabetes mellitus diagnosed in adolescence.

Current Medications: insulin lispro pre-meal sliding scale, glargine 24 units nightly.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 84 bpm, visual acuity 20/60 OD, 20/40 OS. Funduscopic exam reveals bilateral microaneurysms. No papilledema.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Diabetic retinopathy with macular edema. Referral to ophthalmology for laser photocoagulation. Tightening of glycemic control prioritized. Patient counseled on importance of glycemic control. Home glucose log to be reviewed at next visit. Diabetic education materials provided.

For patient handover, the following personal information has been compiled:
Patient Name: Eugene Cooper
Patient ID: PID-00701
Phone: (900) 600-2100
Email: eugene.cooper@gmail.com

CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 52-year-old male presenting with right knee pain after a fall at home that began approximately two days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as progressive and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for previous transient ischemic attack and carotid stenosis.

Current Medications: clopidogrel 75 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 138/82 mmHg, heart rate 76 bpm. Right knee with effusion, decreased range of motion, and tenderness over the medial joint line. Negative Lachman test.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Suspected medial meniscus tear, MRI scheduled. Conservative management with physical therapy initiated. Anti-inflammatory therapy adjusted. Activity modification advised pending imaging results. Knee bracing recommended. Follow-up in two weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 69-year-old female presenting with intermittent diarrhea and abdominal cramping that began approximately five days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as mild and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for stage 4 chronic kidney disease with prior hemodialysis.

Current Medications: darbepoetin alfa weekly, sevelamer 800 mg TID, cinacalcet 30 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 102/64 mmHg, heart rate 88 bpm, weight loss of 6 kg over three months. Abdomen with diffuse mild tenderness. Bowel sounds hyperactive.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Likely irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea predominance. Empirical dietary modification and trial of low-dose antispasmodic. Stool studies pending. Symptom diary requested for next visit. Trigger food list reviewed. Patient instructed to call for worsening abdominal pain or hematochezia.

For patient handover, the following personal information has been compiled:
Patient Name: Eugene Bell
Patient ID: PID-00703
Phone: (902) 614-2126
Email: eugene.bell@outlook.com

CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 45-year-old male presenting with frequent urination and unintentional weight loss that began approximately five days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as severe and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for long-standing migraine with aura.

Current Medications: topiramate 50 mg BID, sumatriptan PRN, propranolol 40 mg BID.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 144/86 mmHg, heart rate 72 bpm. Generalized petechiae on lower extremities. Liver and spleen non-palpable. Cervical lymphadenopathy noted.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Anemia of chronic disease with concurrent thrombocytopenia. Hematology consult requested. Iron studies and erythropoietin level ordered. Bone marrow biopsy considered if cytopenias persist. Iron repletion to begin if deficiency confirmed. Hematology follow-up arranged.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 79-year-old male presenting with recurrent epistaxis and easy bruising that began approximately one week ago. The patient describes the symptoms as mild and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for irritable bowel syndrome and lactose intolerance.

Current Medications: loperamide PRN, dicyclomine 10 mg QID, peppermint oil enteric capsules.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, heart rate 80 bpm. Reduced sensation in stocking-glove distribution. Resting tremor of the right hand. Mild rigidity on passive movement.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Progression of Parkinson disease motor symptoms. Levodopa dose adjusted. Physical therapy referral for gait training. Speech therapy evaluation recommended. Fall risk assessment completed. Family caregiver instructed on home safety modifications.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 75-year-old female presenting with chronic constipation and bloating that began approximately the past 48 hours ago. The patient describes the symptoms as moderate and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for ulcerative colitis in clinical remission.

Current Medications: mesalamine 4.8 g daily, vitamin B12 injections monthly, calcium 600 mg BID.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, heart rate 80 bpm. Reduced sensation in stocking-glove distribution. Resting tremor of the right hand. Mild rigidity on passive movement.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Progression of Parkinson disease motor symptoms. Levodopa dose adjusted. Physical therapy referral for gait training. Speech therapy evaluation recommended. Fall risk assessment completed. Family caregiver instructed on home safety modifications.

CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 69-year-old female presenting with blurred vision and worsening visual disturbance that began approximately one week ago. The patient describes the symptoms as moderate and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for type 1 diabetes mellitus diagnosed in adolescence.

Current Medications: insulin lispro pre-meal sliding scale, glargine 24 units nightly.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 84 bpm, visual acuity 20/60 OD, 20/40 OS. Funduscopic exam reveals bilateral microaneurysms. No papilledema.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Diabetic retinopathy with macular edema. Referral to ophthalmology for laser photocoagulation. Tightening of glycemic control prioritized. Patient counseled on importance of glycemic control. Home glucose log to be reviewed at next visit. Diabetic education materials provided.

CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 69-year-old female presenting with right knee pain after a fall at home that began approximately the past 24 hours ago. The patient describes the symptoms as progressive and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for previous transient ischemic attack and carotid stenosis.

Current Medications: clopidogrel 75 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 138/82 mmHg, heart rate 76 bpm. Right knee with effusion, decreased range of motion, and tenderness over the medial joint line. Negative Lachman test.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Suspected medial meniscus tear, MRI scheduled. Conservative management with physical therapy initiated. Anti-inflammatory therapy adjusted. Activity modification advised pending imaging results. Knee bracing recommended. Follow-up in two weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 37-year-old male presenting with intermittent diarrhea and abdominal cramping that began approximately one week ago. The patient describes the symptoms as progressive and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for stage 4 chronic kidney disease with prior hemodialysis.

Current Medications: darbepoetin alfa weekly, sevelamer 800 mg TID, cinacalcet 30 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 102/64 mmHg, heart rate 88 bpm, weight loss of 6 kg over three months. Abdomen with diffuse mild tenderness. Bowel sounds hyperactive.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Likely irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea predominance. Empirical dietary modification and trial of low-dose antispasmodic. Stool studies pending. Symptom diary requested for next visit. Trigger food list reviewed. Patient instructed to call for worsening abdominal pain or hematochezia.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 47-year-old male presenting with frequent urination and unintentional weight loss that began approximately four days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as severe and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for long-standing migraine with aura.

Current Medications: topiramate 50 mg BID, sumatriptan PRN, propranolol 40 mg BID.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 144/86 mmHg, heart rate 72 bpm. Generalized petechiae on lower extremities. Liver and spleen non-palpable. Cervical lymphadenopathy noted.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Anemia of chronic disease with concurrent thrombocytopenia. Hematology consult requested. Iron studies and erythropoietin level ordered. Bone marrow biopsy considered if cytopenias persist. Iron repletion to begin if deficiency confirmed. Hematology follow-up arranged.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 80-year-old male presenting with right knee pain after a fall at home that began approximately five days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as moderate and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for previous transient ischemic attack and carotid stenosis.

Current Medications: clopidogrel 75 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 138/82 mmHg, heart rate 76 bpm. Right knee with effusion, decreased range of motion, and tenderness over the medial joint line. Negative Lachman test.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Suspected medial meniscus tear, MRI scheduled. Conservative management with physical therapy initiated. Anti-inflammatory therapy adjusted. Activity modification advised pending imaging results. Knee bracing recommended. Follow-up in two weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 84-year-old female presenting with recurrent epistaxis and easy bruising that began approximately five days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as moderate and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Chief Complaint: The patient is a 69-year-old female presenting with tinnitus and progressive hearing loss that began approximately three days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as moderate and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for psoriasis with episodic flares.

Current Medications: calcipotriene topical BID, methotrexate 10 mg weekly, folate 1 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 84 bpm, visual acuity 20/60 OD, 20/40 OS. Funduscopic exam reveals bilateral microaneurysms. No papilledema.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Diabetic retinopathy with macular edema. Referral to ophthalmology for laser photocoagulation. Tightening of glycemic control prioritized. Patient counseled on importance of glycemic control. Home glucose log to be reviewed at next visit. Diabetic education materials provided.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 57-year-old female presenting with reflux symptoms unresponsive to antacids that began approximately the past 48 hours ago. The patient describes the symptoms as severe and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for Parkinson's disease with mild bradykinesia.

Current Medications: carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID, pramipexole 0.5 mg TID, amantadine 100 mg BID.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 144/86 mmHg, heart rate 72 bpm. Generalized petechiae on lower extremities. Liver and spleen non-palpable. Cervical lymphadenopathy noted.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Anemia of chronic disease with concurrent thrombocytopenia. Hematology consult requested. Iron studies and erythropoietin level ordered. Bone marrow biopsy considered if cytopenias persist. Iron repletion to begin if deficiency confirmed. Hematology follow-up arranged.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting with chronic constipation and bloating that began approximately one week ago. The patient describes the symptoms as severe and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

Past Medical History: Significant for ulcerative colitis in clinical remission.

Current Medications: mesalamine 4.8 g daily, vitamin B12 injections monthly, calcium 600 mg BID.

CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting with blurred vision and worsening visual disturbance that began approximately five days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as mild and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for type 1 diabetes mellitus diagnosed in adolescence.

Current Medications: insulin lispro pre-meal sliding scale, glargine 24 units nightly.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 84 bpm, visual acuity 20/60 OD, 20/40 OS. Funduscopic exam reveals bilateral microaneurysms. No papilledema.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Diabetic retinopathy with macular edema. Referral to ophthalmology for laser photocoagulation. Tightening of glycemic control prioritized. Patient counseled on importance of glycemic control. Home glucose log to be reviewed at next visit. Diabetic education materials provided.

CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 69-year-old female presenting with right knee pain after a fall at home that began approximately several days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as severe and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for previous transient ischemic attack and carotid stenosis.

Current Medications: clopidogrel 75 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 138/82 mmHg, heart rate 76 bpm. Right knee with effusion, decreased range of motion, and tenderness over the medial joint line. Negative Lachman test.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Suspected medial meniscus tear, MRI scheduled. Conservative management with physical therapy initiated. Anti-inflammatory therapy adjusted. Activity modification advised pending imaging results. Knee bracing recommended. Follow-up in two weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 40-year-old female presenting with intermittent diarrhea and abdominal cramping that began approximately several days ago. The patient describes the symptoms as moderate and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for stage 4 chronic kidney disease with prior hemodialysis.

Current Medications: darbepoetin alfa weekly, sevelamer 800 mg TID, cinacalcet 30 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 102/64 mmHg, heart rate 88 bpm, weight loss of 6 kg over three months. Abdomen with diffuse mild tenderness. Bowel sounds hyperactive.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Likely irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea predominance. Empirical dietary modification and trial of low-dose antispasmodic. Stool studies pending. Symptom diary requested for next visit. Trigger food list reviewed. Patient instructed to call for worsening abdominal pain or hematochezia.

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 64-year-old female presenting with frequent urination and unintentional weight loss that began approximately the past 24 hours ago. The patient describes the symptoms as severe and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for long-standing migraine with aura.

Current Medications: topiramate 50 mg BID, sumatriptan PRN, propranolol 40 mg BID.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 144/86 mmHg, heart rate 72 bpm. Generalized petechiae on lower extremities. Liver and spleen non-palpable. Cervical lymphadenopathy noted.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Anemia of chronic disease with concurrent thrombocytopenia. Hematology consult requested. Iron studies and erythropoietin level ordered. Bone marrow biopsy considered if cytopenias persist. Iron repletion to begin if deficiency confirmed. Hematology follow-up arranged.

CLINICAL NOTE

Chief Complaint: The patient is a 83-year-old male presenting with tinnitus and progressive hearing loss that began approximately one week ago. The patient describes the symptoms as progressive and reports they have been interfering with daily activities.

History of Present Illness: The onset was gradual with no identifiable precipitating factor. The patient denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or changes in medications. Associated symptoms include occasional fatigue and reduced appetite. The patient reports partial relief with over-the-counter medications.

Past Medical History: Significant for psoriasis with episodic flares.

Current Medications: calcipotriene topical BID, methotrexate 10 mg weekly, folate 1 mg daily.

Physical Examination: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 84 bpm, visual acuity 20/60 OD, 20/40 OS. Funduscopic exam reveals bilateral microaneurysms. No papilledema.

Assessment and Plan: Impression: Diabetic retinopathy with macular edema. Referral to ophthalmology for laser photocoagulation. Tightening of glycemic control prioritized. Patient counseled on importance of glycemic control. Home glucose log to be reviewed at next visit. Diabetic education materials provided.
